frequency_question: How often do structural market frictions or operational limits prevent a scaling program from reaching its target throughput within the designated window?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign or central bank large-scale asset purchase, buyback, or liquidity injection programs with explicit volume ramp-up targets over a defined horizon. Excludes emergency crisis lending facilities.

cases.name: US Treasury Buyback Program Initial Phase 2024

provenance_note: 8 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 8 named; believed roughly 10 major comparable instances total globally in modern monetary policy history.
known_gaps: Excludes minor emerging market central bank operations due to data comparability.
skeleton: 8 successful structural scale-ups out of 10 major historical institutional liquidity adjustment programs where operational capacity and structural friction were tested.
multiplier: 8 / 10 instances reached their operational throughput goals without structural friction capping the program prematurely.
validity_reason: Institutional mechanics of sovereign debt management and primary dealer operations evolve slowly over multi-decade horizons.
